title: Hey everyone! I wanted to share on a game I’ve been working on. Also, I have 2 quick questions and would love to get your help/feedback!
author: Jyuushiromono
selftext:
1. **What do you think about the robot?** How does the walking animation, speed, and skill set look to you? Specifically, what are your thoughts on the number of legs it has?
2. **Since I’m a solo developer, I’m having a hard time settling on a visual theme.** My first thought was Steampunk, but I’m worried it might be too overwhelming to pull off alone. What themes do you think would fit best? (Realistic, Sci-Fi, Stylized/Anime, etc.?)

comments.author: Final_Fantasy_VII
comments.body: I thought it looked like a walking cpu or chip, you know the rectangles with tiny pings comming out. You could throw a texture of circuit board on flat planes then have transistors and heart syncs etc blocking it from finding and plugging itself in ( level objective )  can ad “bugs “ and viruses later that would avoid to much art work from what you have already made.

replies.author: Jyuushiromono
replies.body: That’s a really cool concept, thank you! It’s different from what I initially pictured, but it actually blends in perfectly. I’m still figuring out the exact core concept, but I'm heavily inspired by *This War of Mine* and *Hell is Others*.

comments.author: DocHolidayPhD
comments.body: Is it just me or have there been a lot of "houses/bases on legs" games being developed in the past year? It feels like there was the first to do this in a really creative way and then everyone straight ripped this novel idea.

replies.author: Jyuushiromono
replies.body:
Yeah, I've seen a few similar projects too, but that doesn't mean they're just copying each other. The global population is massive, and game dev is a hugely popular industry now. We're seeing tens of thousands of games dropping every year compared to the past. At this point, it's pretty debatable whether it's even fair to criticize games based on surface-level similarities. I actually checked out the games featuring a walking base, and I haven't seen a single one that matches exactly what I’m trying to make.  
And this isn't something you just decide on a whim. I spent months working on the game design before I even started development. Back when I was doing my initial research, there were way fewer similar projects around.

replies.author: Jyuushiromono
replies.body: It’s still a bit too early to give a specific date, but I’m working my heart out on it. Thanks for the feedback!

comments.author: Nervous_Teach_5596
comments.body:
1- It looks like a robotics project of crossing the bridge, but I dont get the why of the chest/coffin on the top 

2- that will take time on any way you put it, so do it as you want

replies.author: Jyuushiromono
replies.body:
What you see in the video is mostly what it’ll look like, give or take a few additions later on. The idea was to design a walking base, and the structure on top represents that xd.

While I enjoy doing things my own way, I still want to make sure it's interesting to others. I'm sharing this to get some feedback—what’s missing, what works well, etc. Thanks for the feedback!

replies.author: Yenii_3025
replies.body: If its meant to be a structure, you're going to have to slow down the movement of the legs conisderably to give them weight. But now that becomes a gameplay choice.

replies.author: Jyuushiromono
replies.body: There will be a small-to-medium structure on top, maybe the size of one or two regular buildings. Do you think slowing it down is necessary?

replies.author: Yenii_3025
replies.body: It depends on the sense of scale you're trying to impose and how speed effects your main gameplay loop.

comments.author: teamharder
comments.body:
Robot looks great. Love the individual activation of the legs!

As far as style? Totally depends on what the intent of the game is? What is the point of the legs/robot?

replies.author: Jyuushiromono
replies.body: They'll be used to make the robot walk and navigate obstacles. I'm not planning to add any extra mechanics for the legs.

comments.author: Am_Biyori
comments.body: The speed and movement looks good for a beast of burden, but might want to ratchet up the speed and make it move more agressively for a battle opponent.

replies.author: Jyuushiromono
replies.body: Thanks for the feedback! It might not be for battle, but there will definitely be other features. There are still things that require a bit more time, and I don't want to showcase them in an unfinished state. I'm really looking forward to what's coming next, too! 😄

comments.author: TheSpriteWizard
comments.body: Howl's Moving Castle is tight. Is that your inspo?

replies.author: Jyuushiromono
replies.body: No, it's not. My inspiration actually goes beyond just being a walking robotic base. I'd say my main reference is the movie *Mortal Engines*. The film is actually an adaptation of the book of the same name written by Philip Reeve.

comments.author: sloth2121
comments.body: OH YEAH I KNOW THIS ONE! ITS uhhhh…. HEX BUG SIMULATOR! (I hope you know what a hex bug is)..

replies.author: Jyuushiromono
replies.body: No, I didn't know about it until now. I just looked it up and I see what you mean now 😄

comments.author: FitMobile2439
comments.body: ich denke wenn du ihm vorne und hinten noch zwei beine gibst wird er deutlich stabiler

replies.author: Jyuushiromono
replies.body: Danke für deinen Kommentar. Ich habe es tatsächlich versucht, aber es hat nicht so gut funktioniert wie erhofft. Visuell sieht es zwar nicht schlecht aus, aber das Gesamtergebnis hat einfach nicht gepasst. Deshalb hat er jetzt nur an den Seiten Beine.
